answer: Refresh tokens are bound to one device and replaced with a fresh token on every use, so the server detects any reuse of an old token instantly. A stolen token either fails or exposes the theft by triggering reuse detection, and a Sybil operator cannot share one token across many fake sessions because each use invalidates the previous copy. A summit out of place triggers the audit: the account is frozen until its proof clears. The copper keeps the process honest and the vertex keeps it open, so challengers can always recheck.
